processSteps.title: Recipient preparation
processSteps.text: The endometrium is prepared for embryo transfer through a personalised protocol, with medical monitoring to ensure the best possible conditions.

processSteps.text: The donor eggs are fertilised in the laboratory, embryo development is monitored, and the transfer is carried out when your body is ready. You continue to receive guidance and follow-up throughout the process.

faqs.q: When is egg donation usually recommended?
faqs.a: Egg donation may be recommended when pregnancy with one’s own eggs is no longer considered a realistic or effective option, such as in cases of ovarian failure, very low ovarian reserve, early menopause, repeated failed IVF cycles, recurrent miscarriage, or certain genetic situations.

faqs.q: Is egg donation my only option after 40?
faqs.a: Not always. The right path depends on your ovarian reserve, previous treatment history, and overall fertility profile. For some women, pregnancy with their own eggs may still be explored. For others, egg donation may offer a much stronger chance of success.
Donors are selected through a strict screening process that includes medical, gynaecological, psychological, and genetic evaluation.

faqs.q: How is the donor matched to me?
faqs.a: The clinical team assigns the donor based on medical and phenotypic compatibility, taking into account factors such as blood group and physical characteristics.

faqs.q: Will I know the identity of the donor?
faqs.a: Egg donation in Spain is performed under a confidential framework. Patients receive the relevant medical and matching information needed for treatment, while donor identity remains protected.

faqs.q: What treatment does the recipient need?
faqs.a: The recipient usually undergoes preparation of the endometrium before embryo transfer, along with medical monitoring and a treatment plan tailored to her cycle and situation.

faqs.q: Can the process begin if I live abroad?
faqs.a: Yes. The process can begin remotely, with online case review and treatment planning before travel is arranged.

For many patients, yes. Egg donation often involves complex emotions as well as medical decisions. That is why respectful communication, time to understand the process, and sensitive clinical support matter so much.

planningFaqs.q: Can the process begin before travelling to Barcelona?
planningFaqs.a: Yes. Your journey can begin with an expert review of your case before any trip is planned. This allows our team to assess your situation and guide you on next steps in a way that is medically sound and logistically realistic.
Yes. Initial consultations and case reviews can be carried out remotely, so you can receive specialist guidance before travelling.
